author: Bjorn Deade
title: Pregnant influencer asks flight attendant to lift her 9-pound bag, claims he refused to help her: 'I was so shocked' - NewsBreak
text:
By Bjorn Deade ,
6 hours ago Image by StockSnap on Pixabay. Pregnant women may need to take extra precautions when traveling by air. Depending on how far along they are, they may face additional travel restrictions and need to be more mindful of physical tasks, particularly when handling luggage and moving through busy airports. One pregnant influencer recently recounted a surprising interaction after asking a flight attendant for assistance with her luggage.
As reported by Fox News , Dominique Elissa, who is currently pregnant, recently appeared on the “Big Small Talk” podcast in early October, where she recounted an encounter with a male flight attendant. She said she was trying to place her carry-on bag, which weighed around 9 pounds, in the overhead compartment. Given her pregnancy, she asked the attendant to help her lift it, expecting him to accommodate her request.
To her dismay, he declined. “I asked the flight attendant, ‘Can you please put my bag above my head? Like, I’m pregnant?’” Elissa recalled. “And then I said, ‘Well, I’m actually pregnant. I’d really appreciate if you could help me because last time I injured myself.’ And he goes, ‘Well, if you’re not able to lift your bag above your head, you have to check it in.’ And I just, yeah, I was just so shocked.”
Another passenger offered to help Elissa Unsure what to do, Elissa began messaging her husband, who reminded her not to carry the bag because she was pregnant. “I was like, I don’t know what to do. I don’t know how to get my bag down because the flight attendant didn’t come and help me.” Fortunately, another passenger noticed her predicament and offered to help. “And the guy next to me, I think he saw my text messages. He’s like, ‘Would you like me to get your bag?’”
In an interview with news.com.au. , the Australian pilates instructor shared more details about her experience. Elissa, who is now nine months pregnant, said the incident occurred a couple of months ago while she was flying from Sydney to Melbourne to spend time with friends. She had traveled to Melbourne the previous week for her first maternity photoshoot.
Beyond her initial shock, Elissa said the encounter left her feeling embarrassed and upset, as she was not accustomed to asking others for help. She also said she experienced significant pain for the following 48 hours. “I have always been a strong, independent woman and pregnancy has been a real lesson in allowing myself to slow down and accept support when I need it,” she said .
Elissa’s experience is not the only recent account of a traveler facing questions from airline staff over pregnancy-related needs. In a separate incident, a Delta passenger carrying a breast pump bag alleged that a gate agent questioned her about where her baby was .
